clue.text: Don't show courage in court

parts.note: bottle is British slang for nerve or courage
someone up before the magistrates is appearing in court

explanation.surface: An instruction to a nervous witness not to reveal any bravery when standing trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't show courage' reads as a call for timidity, but it is the whole definition: keep feelings hidden. Bottle is British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep feelings suppressed and hidden is the idiom meaning not to let them be seen.

clue.text: Extremely fat old workers finding some energy lowered

indicators.note: in a down entry, lowering a letter moves it further down the column, towards the end

parts.note: bees are the classic workers of the hive
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Elderly labourers who have grown very overweight because they have lost some of their get-up-and-go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowered' moves the second E of BEES down to the end, making BESE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grossly overweight people are described medically by this adjective, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Delighted snooker player's made fine shot?

definitions.meaning: in snooker a delicate shot that just touches the pink ball could be described as having lightly brushed it

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker the pink is one of the coloured balls; a fine shot barely grazes the object ball.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being extremely pleased, as if flushed with pleasure, is this colourful phrase.

clue.text: Infant upsets me and cockney girl's fella

indicators.note: in a down entry, upsetting a word turns it upside down, so it reads from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
her, with the cockney dropped h, is 'er
a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: A baby causes trouble for the speaker and for a London woman's boyfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' turns ME into EM. A cockney drops the H of 'her', leaving 'ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something emerging, just coming into existence, is in its infancy, so infant works as an adjective.

clue.text: Nasty piece of work involving rotten people and sin

indicators.note: involved means tangled or convoluted, so the following words are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vile individual mixed up with corrupt folk and wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nasty piece of work' suggests a person, but here it is a spiteful anonymous letter. ROTTEN, PEOPLE and SIN are rearranged; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: An anonymous malicious letter is literally a nasty piece of written work.

clue.text: Phone from American city

explanation.definitionFit: British English calls a cellphone by this name, and it is also a city in Alabama.

clue.text: Slight cuts in income agreed

indicators.note: the answer cuts in across the boundary of the following words, lying inside them

explanation.surface: Small reductions in earnings have been accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight cuts' looks like a phrase about small reductions, but 'Slight' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scanty or small in amount is slight, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Pick up bill in club

indicators.note: in a down entry, picking a word up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar

explanation.surface: Collecting the bill at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' turns TAB to read upwards; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or baseball bat is a club used for striking the ball.

clue.text: Uniformed servant, irritable with staff

parts.note: livery is an old word for irritable or liverish
to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: A grumpy footman in uniform, along with the household employees.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVERY, like liverish, means bad-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant wearing his master's livery, the distinctive dress, is so named.

clue.text: Green sack used regularly for delivery

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter from the words in front

explanation.surface: An environmentally friendly bag reused for bringing post to the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is part of the letter run: every second letter of GREEN SACK USED.
explanation.definitionFit: A delivery can mean a release or saving from danger, as in deliverance.

clue.text: Current Conservative leader clothed by mother still

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: being clothed by means being wrapped inside what follows

parts.note: native, as in mother tongue or mother country

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Tory chief kept wrapped up by their mum remains motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: C (leader of Conservative) is clothed by NATIVE to give NACTIVE, after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being still means not moving, which is to be idle or not active.

clue.text: Get better tip, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken and the sound matters

parts.note: to heel is to tip over or list, of a ship

explanation.surface: A request for better advice.
explanation.walkthrough: A ship heels when it tips over to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover from an injury or illness is to mend, to become well again.

clue.text: Last and best ever in state, officially

parts.note: to last is to continue or go on
a record is the best performance ever achieved

explanation.surface: Final and greatest of all time in the nation, formally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like an adjective but is the verb go on; 'state' is a verb too, not a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare something publicly and formally is the idiom meaning to state for the record.

clue.text: Violent onset of cyclone disrupted a city's calm

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter
disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken with its s as letters

explanation.surface: A storm's arrival has shattered the peace of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: C (the onset of cyclone) comes first, then A CITYS CALM is rearranged to ATACLYSMIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A cataclysm is a violent upheaval, so the adjective describes something violently destructive.

clue.text: Not welcoming game when snow may fall?

parts.note: a cold reception is an unfriendly one
snap is a children's card game

explanation.surface: An unfriendly game played in wintry weather.
explanation.walkthrough: SNAP is a card game where players shout when two matching cards turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden short spell of freezing weather is the time snow might fall, defined by example.

clue.text: Female slave quailed so, getting thrashed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman in bondage cowered as she was whipped.
explanation.definitionFit: A concubine or slave girl in a Turkish harem is the meaning of this exotic word.

clue.text: Bird — it may be Central European

explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving a jail sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison slang for a sentence is this word, and CET is a time zone.

clue.text: Boss is going round university reading a lot

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Famous poem about heartless artist

explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Dalí was the Spanish Surrealist painter, so artist is a definition by example.

clue.text: Spotting disguise of mostly incognito characters

explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last O of INCOGNITO, leaving INCOGNIT to rearrange; 'characters' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotting something is seeing or observing it, a present-participle synonym.

clue.text: Plan he abandons finally

parts.note: finally means at last, in the end
taken as written

clue.text: King stops destruction of Hebridean port

clue.text: Hindu philosophy's rejection of a Gentile

clue.text: Reportedly what dazzles as naturally-produced adhesive?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the sound matters

parts.note: a glare is a dazzling light

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: the substance is egg white.

clue.text: Extremely conservative and fair, by the way

parts.note: a square deal is a fair one

explanation.definitionFit: A square is a conventional, old-fashioned person, so the superlative means most conservative.

clue.text: Top need for colonist

parts.note: want means need or lack

clue.text: Enthusiasm about a brass band's sound

clue.text: Easy assignment that can make others smoke
